review.assessment: The change modifies `sla.py` to use `st.is_terminal(job.status)` instead of an explicit check for `(DONE, FAILED)`. This relies on `status.py` correctly identifying `CANCELLED` as a terminal status (where the clock stops). If the status module was updated with the new vocabulary but the logic in `is_terminal` was not correspondingly updated to include it, cancelled jobs will still be treated as active. The comment asserts cancellation is included, but without seeing `status.py`, this remains an unverified dependency that could perpetuate the SLA reporting error.

findings.actual: If st.is_terminal excludes CANCELLED, finished_at returns now (current time), causing cancelled jobs to accrue infinite SLA time.
findings.defect: Reliance on `st.is_terminal` for determining if the clock stops on a job. If the status module does not include CANCELLED in its definition of terminal statuses, this function will return `now` instead of `ended_at`, causing cancelled jobs to continue accruing SLA time indefinitely.
findings.expected: Cancelled jobs should stop accruing SLA time at their `ended_at` timestamp.
